reviewer: agent visual inspection; no independent designer signoff

observations.sandbox: Inspector section boundaries, paired inputs and alignment glyphs share the existing rhythm; artwork remains authored. Extreme controls stack or truncate within narrow columns.
observations.spline: Transform labels and numeric controls align; source materials are retained. At the extreme case the inspector moves below the scene.
observations.webflow: Style controls share common field height, text and section padding; canvas remains authored. Extreme toolbar wraps and local sections require scrolling.
observations.framer: Position and Size sections share the existing Accordion/field rhythm in both themes. Extreme column widths leave little canvas space; this is not certified as comfortable UX.
observations.workflow: Node inspector field boundaries and spacing agree with other panels; executor remains an explicitly local fixture.
observations.chat: Metadata panel, result icons and composer retain common slots/foreground; the transcript is source content, not a connected AI response.
observations.building: Document/editor controls and source artwork are retained; no new inspector invented.
observations.recents: Files baseline retains shared control/icon rhythm; colored thumbnails/logos are not converted into monochrome glyphs.
observations.slider: Single/range rails, values and native focus rings are coherent with actual neighboring SEDA controls in both themes. Numeric core extraction does not change painted JS/CSS output.

limits: Extreme simultaneous XL/150%/X24/Y12 settings are visually crowded; local scrolling, stacked controls and ellipsis remain necessary.
Geometry PASS is not proof of comfortable UX at all combinations.
No fresh Figma fidelity, target OS/AT/touch screen reader, Firefox/WebKit or native desktop certification.
Authored document/canvas typography is not replaced by application density parameters.
